## Things the offline runs showed that the page flags as Watch items (not claimed as bugs)
1. Live tab's Groups line still prints "gap 5-20 days" (the v6 jitter) while the clock is adaptive (Layers: "adapt 0.5-20d"). Step 2.5.
2. The window's Ledger K filter has no kind for panic, lead, adopt, size, strand, eco, extinct; roster builds log as kind
   `roster` but the filter offers `build`. Steps 2.10, 6.8.
3. Alt+H vocabulary unchanged from v7.0 (A3 14.3 not fixed; Panel per-control help covers it). Step 6.7.
4. `irruption now 1` with nothing to send moved a pinned pressure 1.00 -> 0.50 (stub world; may be an artifact). Step 5.9.
5. `perf` raised on the stubbed DFHack perf counters (a table where a number is expected); almost certainly a stub
   artifact. Step 6.11. (`roster build` also raised offline: a stub numeric field; not flagged.)
6. CACHE.release still reads 7.0.0 at fce7d68 (the docs stream is bumping it). Step 0.4 expects 7.1.0 and says what 7.0.0 means.
7. ui.md calls Alpha Three's Layers steps "11.3/11.4"; they are 12.1/12.2 on the Alpha Three page.
8. The formula cap is floor(sqrt(embark tiles)) + 1: a 1x1 embark holds 2 groups per layer (the stubbed harness showed 2),
   3x3 holds 4, 4x4 holds 5. The b1-forts programme embarks 1x1s, so step 0.1 asks testers for a 3x3 or larger embark;
   R45's 3-5 water groups cannot be reached on a 1x1.

## The playtest page (R62): proposal, nothing regenerated
The old "Seasonal Wildlife Playtest" (`.claude/scratch/seasonal-wildlife-playtest.html`, 10 MB, built by
`scripts/validate-report.py` from one validate-full run) is a validator report: 176 claims by verdict, 51 screenshots inlined
as JPEG data URIs. It answers "did the rig's claims pass", not "does a player see what the design says".

**Proposal: retire it as a separate artifact and make Alpha Four's page the one results view**, in three parts:
1. **One page, two evidence columns per step.** Each Alpha Four step already names its validator claims in Basis
   (gui.panel.set, web.set, mech.v71.*). Add a second loader beside "Load a round": paste a validate-full `results.json`;
   each step shows the verdicts of the claims it cites (PASS/FAIL/NOT-TESTABLE chips) next to the tester's mark.
   A step with a tester Pass and a claim FAIL (or the reverse) is the interesting row; the report lists those first.
2. **No inlined screenshots.** Link a screenshot only for anomalies, by run id and file name (the run dir keeps them),
   or embed small crops of the screen-dump text instead (text is a few KB; it is also what the screen checks parse).
   That keeps the page under 1 MB instead of 10.
3. **The backlog, doc-drift and "what it costs" sections** of the old page move into phase 7 ("What this page cannot
   check") as a short table fed from the same results.json (counts only), so nothing the old page showed is lost.
Cost: the validator must first carry v7.1 claims (the stream notes list ~80 new ids) and run on r2
(revalidate-dfhack-r2, then validate-full). Until then the old page describes v6.x-v7.0 on r1.1 and should not be
republished. Decision for the user: retire the old artifact (or leave it as a v7.0 record) once Alpha Four's results view
has its first round.
